newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling eases vs dlr on corporate interest.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling eases vs dlr on corporate interest.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened marginally against the dollar on Thursday on increased dollar buying interest from corporate importers and the Central Bank of Kenya, commercial bank dealers said.
The central bank posted a mean of 55.34 shillings to the dollar from 55.33 on Wednesday. It was posted unchanged against sterling at 91.04 shillings.

Some dealers said foreign exchange from export sales continued to stream in and cause the shilling to firm, but matching demand from importers and the central bank held the shilling within the 55.30 to 55.40 range.
"The shilling weakened marginally when the central bank came in late on Wednesday afternoon buying dollars at the 55.35 level," one dealer said.
Another dealer said the interbank market was fairly active in cross-currency trading.
Dealers saw the shilling trading within the 55.30/40 range until the weekend without any significant factors expecte to move the market.
The money market was still liquid as traders piled money in, anticipating tighter rates next week. Overnight rates were quoted as high as 12 percent from between five and ten percent on Wednesday.
